title: ZTIE REJECT/hold disposition data contract (v1)
description: The derived, bounded REJECT/hold DISPOSITION OUTCOME produced by the Story 4.7 enforcement mechanism (RD-047, per RD-048/RD-049), and the ELEVENTH envelope kind on the Forensic -> Hub RD-013 gate. On a VERIFIED Hub-signed `rejected` decision token (verified OFFLINE — never the advisory recommended_verdict, RD-040), the Forensic-side destroyer tears down the raw artifact (all S3 versions + delete-markers under intake/<intake_id>/) + its derived Forensic outputs (findings/ runs/ traces/) AND terminates any live detonation chamber (explicit, not TTL); it then crosses THIS bounded outcome back to the Hub. It records the mechanism `outcome` (destroyed / held / refused_not_rejected / refused_hash_mismatch — FAIL-SAFE: only 'destroyed' means anything was torn down; 'held' is the INCONCLUSIVE/no-token default and destroys NOTHING), the human decision observed on the token, whether the sha256 verified, the chamber state, that the derived report SURVIVES in the Hub, and — only when destroyed — bounded facts about what was torn down (version count, prefixes, chamber). Nothing raw crosses (RD-009/RD-013). It is NOT a verdict: there is NO verdict/safe/approved/forward/pass_fail/malicious/clean field anywhere; `outcome` is the MECHANISM result, the DECISION was the human reject, and the verdict is human-gated. Allow-list: additionalProperties false at every level; every field typed and enum/length/range-bounded. Integrity-keyed by intake_id + sha256. DERIVED-ONLY. OWN version pin (DISPOSITION_CONTRACT_VERSION) + a UNIQUE 'disposition' discriminator that does not collide with any other envelope kind.

contract_version.description: REJECT/hold-disposition-contract schema version. Pinned SEPARATELY on the Hub validator (DISPOSITION_CONTRACT_VERSION) so this envelope kind versions independently of the other ten kinds (never rides the shared CONTRACT_VERSION). The Hub rejects unknown-version envelopes fail-closed.

intake_id.description: The intake UUIDv4 this disposition outcome is for. The Hub upserts the outcome onto the tracking record keyed by this.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw artifact body. Integrity key, bound to intake_id; the Hub rejects a disposition outcome whose sha256 does not match the tracked record. On a destroy this is the same hash the mechanism verified against the token before destroying (SI-7); on a hold it is the recomputed artifact hash (or the tracked hash echoed) so the outcome still binds to the record.

disposed_at.description: RFC3339/ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (Z-suffixed) the disposition mechanism produced this outcome in Forensic (the time of the reject attempt, destroy or hold or refusal).

disposition.description: The bounded REJECT/hold DISPOSITION OUTCOME: what the Story 4.7 mechanism did for this intake. It records the mechanism `outcome` (destroyed / held / refused_not_rejected / refused_hash_mismatch), the human decision it observed on the presented token (EVIDENCE of what gated the action), whether the sha256 verified, whether the derived report survives (always true — the Hub record is untouched), the chamber state, and — only when destroyed — bounded facts about what was torn down. EVIDENCE only; NO verdict anywhere. `outcome` is the mechanism result, NOT a safety judgement; the decision was the human reject (a Hub-signed token).

outcome.description: What the reject/hold mechanism did. 'destroyed' = a verified Hub-signed `rejected` token + a matching sha256, so the raw artifact (all versions) + its derived Forensic outputs were destroyed and any live chamber was terminated (the ONLY outcome where anything was torn down). 'held' = FAIL-SAFE, no `rejected` token presented (INCONCLUSIVE / pending), nothing destroyed. 'refused_not_rejected' / 'refused_hash_mismatch' = FAIL-CLOSED, a token was presented but did not authorize a destroy, nothing destroyed. NEVER a safety verdict.

observed_decision.description: The human decision the mechanism observed on the presented token. EVIDENCE of what gated the action — the destroy happens ONLY on a verified 'rejected' token (RD-040/RD-047: the advisory recommended_verdict is NEVER the trigger). 'pending' = no `rejected` token was presented (the hold path). The decision itself is a Hub-signed token, human-owned, produced by the Phase-4 gate (Story 4.4), never by 4.7.

hash_verified.description: True iff the recomputed Forensic sha256 matched the presented token's sha256 (SI-7 integrity + artifact binding). A destroy happens ONLY when this is true (among the other checks); false records a fail-closed integrity refusal. On a pure hold (no token) this is false (no artifact binding was checked).

chamber_state.description: The detonation chamber state observed by the mechanism: 'terminated' / 'none_running' when a destroy ran (the chamber was inspected), or 'not_checked' on a hold / refusal (nothing is destroyed, so the chamber is deliberately left to its hard TTL).

report_survives.description: Always true. The derived report + the durable tracking record live in the Hub (RD-012) and are NEVER touched by 4.7 — only the Forensic blast-zone artifact + chamber are destroyed. Recorded explicitly so the audit trail affirms the report survives a reject.

destroyed.description: Bounded facts about what the mechanism tore down in Forensic when outcome is 'destroyed': how many S3 object versions (+ delete-markers) were deleted under the intake's prefixes, which prefixes were cleared, and the detonation chamber state. A COUNT + prefix list, never a per-object listing and never the payload (RD-009). Present only when outcome is 'destroyed'.

artifact_versions_deleted.description: Total number of S3 object versions AND delete-markers deleted across all of the intake's Forensic prefixes (the versioned bucket requires deleting every version + marker — a plain delete leaves versions). A bounded count, never content.

prefixes_cleared.description: The Forensic S3 key prefixes that were destroyed for this intake (e.g. intake/<id>/, findings/<id>/, runs/<id>/, traces/<id>/). POINTERS into Forensic — never the payload. Bounded list.

chamber.description: The detonation chamber (ephemeral Story-2.3 EC2) state for this intake at reject time: 'terminated' (a live host was found and explicitly terminated, not waiting for the TTL), or 'none_running' (no live host — the common case, the hard TTL already reaped it).

chamber_instance_id.description: Optional EC2 instance id of the live chamber that was terminated (present only when chamber is 'terminated'), for traceability. A bounded identifier, never content.

destroyed_at.description: Optional RFC3339/ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (Z-suffixed) the destroy completed in Forensic. Present when outcome is 'destroyed'.

artifact_s3_key.description: Optional Forensic S3 key of the raw artifact the reject decision was about (intake/<intake_id>/<filename>), for traceability. A pointer into Forensic — never the payload.

reason.description: Optional short, bounded, non-executable reason for a hold / refusal (e.g. 'no rejected decision token presented (hold at approval gate)' or 'wrong_decision: decision \'accepted\' != required \'rejected\''). Never raw content, never a verdict.
